title: Directional token floors + streaming grace-credit experiment for public API
creator: Lena Zhao
description:
Objective: Validate a directional (input vs output) per-token floor plus a streaming-specific grace-credit model to reduce invoice volatility for enterprise customers while preserving revenue from high-output workloads. We want a mechanism that: 1) Applies asymmetric minimums (separate monthly floors) for ingress and egress tokens, 2) Offers a streaming grace window to avoid penalizing handshakes/reconnects and short-lived interactive sessions, and 3) Measures churn/elasticity and revenue impact across Small, Mid, and Enterprise cohorts.

Hypotheses:
- H1: Splitting floors by direction reduces customer complaints for high-input workloads (fine-tuning/data ingestion) while maintaining revenue capture from output-heavy apps (chatbots, summarizers).
- H2: A small per-minute streaming grace-credit significantly reduces overbilling complaints for interactive apps without materially reducing MRR.
- H3: Combining directional floors with a streaming grace preserves fairness and simplifies invoicing for enterprise contract terms.

Experiment design:
- Variant A (Control): Current unified monthly floor (baseline).
- Variant B (Directional Floors): Separate ingress and egress monthly minimums (eg. $X ingress floor, $Y egress floor) with identical unit rates to baseline.
- Variant C (Directional + Grace): Variant B + streaming grace-credit policy (first N streaming minutes per day per workspace free up to a credit cap).
- Segment cohorts: Small (< $1k/mo), Mid ($1k-$25k/mo), Enterprise (> $25k/mo). Randomize new signups + opt-in pilot customers with notification and feedback form.

Metrics & instrumentation:
- Primary: Revenue delta (net MRR change), churn rate at 30/60 days, dispute incidence (billing disputes opened), support tickets labeled ‘billing-streaming’ or ‘directional-floor’.
- Secondary: Average egress vs ingress token ratio per customer, sessions dropped due to grace exhaustion, median latency impact (should be none), conversion to reserved commits.
- Telemetry events required: token_count.direction, streaming_session.start/stop, streaming_reconnect, grace_credit.applied, floor_billing.triggered, billing_dispute.opened. (See telemetry spec link).

Rollout plan:
- Week 0: PRD and legal check; instrument telemetry; create billing simulator job to project outcomes using 6 months of historical traffic.
- Week 1: Implement billing rules behind feature flag; internal QA with billing-team test tenants; fetch simulator outputs.
- Week 2: Soft launch to pilot Enterprise customers (3 customers from SE book) + 5% random sample of Mid cohort. Monitor for 72 hours.
- Week 3-4: Iterate pricing amounts and grace window based on simulator + pilot feedback. Broaden to 20% of Mid and 10% of Small if stable.
- Post-experiment: Evaluate 60-day revenue/churn impact; draft recommended permanent pricing change or runway for more experiments.

Risks & guardrails:
- Legal/Contract risk: Contracts that already reference ‘monthly token minimum’ must be respected. Legal to approve fallback language.
- Accounting complexity: Need to ensure invoices map to existing GL account structure. Finance to validate revenue recognition.
- Support load: Pre-write support playbook and automated invoice breakdown.
- Gaming risk: Customers may shift traffic to exploit grace window. Introduce rate-limit and per-workspace cap.

Deliverables:
- PRD (Drive): Drive doc with simulator outputs and expected P&L scenarios.
- Billing simulator: Notebook + 6-month backtest.
- Telemetry spec: Event definitions and Grafana dashboards.
- Support KB: Messaging templates and dispute triage flow.

Notes on enterprise questionnaire and security alignment:
- For customers requesting SQ updates (security questionnaires), add explanatory language describing that directional floors and grace credits are billing constructs only and do not change data residency, retention, or access controls. Coordinate with Security to prepare a FAQ snippet for RFP/SQ responses.

Links: See links field for PRD, simulator notebook, and billing spec.
